title: Embody the Phase 2 zero-copy SRAM packet endpoint
hypothesis: A finite descriptor-driven endpoint can sustain segmented 256-bit traffic without packet-wide registers while making source retention, SRAM backpressure, packet metadata, receive context, direct writes, and completion control physically measurable.

direct_comparison.primary_question: What PPA and service constraints replace the Phase 2 model's uncosted zero-copy descriptor and packetizer abstraction?

expected_benefit: replace logical zero-copy release queues with finite RTL
measure endpoint timing, area, and vectorless power
expose sustainable SRAM-to-NoC service constraints for the Llama7B reroute
risks: the compact harness adds disclosed source/observation logic
SRAM latency and energy remain external until macro composition
vectorless PPA does not provide workload activity energy

required_evaluations.objective: Measure Nangate45 PPA for the concrete Phase 2 descriptor-driven SRAM packet endpoint.
